method_note: Read the whole target file. Chose claims by impact on a test oracle: GS1 resolver status codes and file names, GS1 Digital Link rules, TDS header values, IANA relation, IDTA discovery endpoints and deprecations, EU legal citations (articles and paragraphs), repository metadata (gh api), NXP SUN constants, ndeflib prefix table, AI rules from the GS1 syntax dictionary, DOIs (Crossref and OpenAlex), and the existing_check statements (compared with src/dppce/adapters/identifier.py and docs/reference/capabilities.md). PDFs were saved by WebFetch and read with pdftotext. No live DPP system was contacted. Checks of the large EU texts used windows of the Cellar manifestations, as the EUR-Lex /eng pages returned empty content to WebFetch in this session.

checked.claim: GS1 Digital Link URI Syntax is release 1.7.0, ratified Aug 2026, PDF dated 2026-08-06.
checked.evidence: Page shows release 1.7.0, ratified Aug 2026, PDF dated 2026-08-06.

checked.claim: GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard is release 1.2.1, ratified Aug 2026 (page typo 'Ratfied'; PDF file name 2026-08-07).
checked.evidence: Page shows 1.2.1, ratified Aug 2026 with the same typo, and the PDF name carries 7 August 2026.

checked.claim: Resolver 1.2.1 returns 404 (not a default redirect) when the requested link type is unavailable (changed from 1.1), 300 for ambiguous best match, 400 on validation failure including check digit, never 200 for errors, and names no redirect status code (301/302/307/308).
checked.evidence: Page text states 404 for an unavailable link type (change from 1.1), 300 when the resolver cannot choose, 400 for failed basic validation (check calculation is one of the tests; the 400 sentence itself does not name check digits), a SHALL NOT use 200 for error conditions, and no redirect code is named. Read through character 100000 of 107148; the last 7148 characters were not read.
checked.correction: Optional precision: the check digit is covered only through the 'basic validation' wording, not by name in the 400 sentence.

checked.claim: Resolver must support GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and CORS; offers gs1:defaultLinkMulti; may expose gs1:handledBy in a Link header; decompresses EPC binary strings; the conformance statement has 25 requirements; description file at /.well-known/gs1resolver.
checked.evidence: All items found on the page: methods and CORS, defaultLinkMulti, handledBy relation, EPC binary decompression required (full Digital Link decompression optional), 25 numbered requirements, and the well-known path gs1resolver.

checked.claim: Qualifier order is 22, 10, 21; GTIN-8/12/13 are zero-padded to 14 digits (mandatory since 1.4.0); linkType and context are reserved query keys; canonical form uses https, id.gs1.org, 14 digits, only AI keys in the query, sorted keys, no trailing slash.
checked.evidence: Page states the same qualifier order, padding requirement effective from 1.4.0, the reserved keys (excluded from canonical URIs) and the canonical rules, including lexical key sorting.

checked.evidence: pdftotext of the saved PDFs shows 'Release 2.3, Ratified, Oct 2025' and 'Release 3.0.1, Ratified, Feb 2026'. The page counts 448 and 204 come from PDF linearization metadata, not from a counted page tree.

checked.claim: UNTP IDR (GitLab main) uses 307 for redirects, 400 for invalid queries, 404 when nothing matches (linkset may be included), 200 for linkset; /.well-known/resolver (or gs1resolver); linkType=all is only a deprecated alias.
checked.evidence: Page states each of these. Read the first 100000 of 105639 characters.

checked.claim: UNTP proposes UUIDs as hard-to-guess item identifiers acting as a shared secret for item data, in conflict with RFC 9562.
checked.evidence: The UNTP page says UUIDs can be useful where being hard to guess matters, for example to limit item data to the genuine holder, and points to a separate access control specification. It does not call them secrets. RFC 9562 section 8 does say UUIDs must not be used as security capabilities and must not be assumed hard to guess, so the tension is real, but 'shared secret' is the file's wording, not UNTP's.
checked.correction: Say: UNTP suggests UUIDs where hard-to-guess values help limit item-data visibility; RFC 9562 warns against relying on UUID unguessability for security. Drop 'shared secret' or tag it as the file's inference.

checked.claim: UNTP uses the non-URN form uuid:{UUID}, not urn:uuid.
checked.evidence: Page gives uuid:{UUID} with an example and does not mention urn:uuid. RFC 9562 gives the urn:uuid form.

rule5_findings.problem: Low risk. The text names ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 1271-36 and MOD 97-10 as the check schemes. Both names come from the Catena-X and LEI ROC pages, and the file does not describe the algorithm. This is naming, not paraphrase.
rule5_findings.fix: No change needed. Keep the 'bibliographic only' tag and do not add algorithm details.

rule5_findings.problem: Low risk. States that IDTA 02099-1 follows (F)prEN 18219:2026 for the format of two elements. This reports what an open IDTA page says about the reference, not what EN 18219 requires.
rule5_findings.fix: No change needed. Keep the wording 'reference noted, content not used'.

rule5_findings.problem: No sentence was found that describes, paraphrases or summarizes the content of an EN, ISO, IEC or DIN document. AAS facts come from IDTA and admin-shell-io, identification link facts from GS1, and battery facts from Regulation (EU) 2023/1542. Search-result scope text for ISO/IEC 18004 was discarded as stated.

missed_items.topic: Registry set-up date in ESPR Art. 13(1)
missed_items.fact: Art. 13(1) sets 19 July 2026 as the date by which the Commission must set up the digital registry. The file says nothing about this date, though 2026/1778 was published on 17 July 2026.

missed_items.topic: Scope of the battery QR code
missed_items.fact: Art. 13(6) of the Batteries Regulation applies the QR code to all batteries from 18 February 2027, but only LMT, industrial above 2 kWh and EV batteries link to the passport. A conformance test for 'QR leads to passport' needs the battery category in the ICS.

Annex III has twelve points (a) to (l); point (l) refers to the service provider that hosts the back-up copy of the passport. Point (c) names GTIN under ISO/IEC 15459-6. Relevant to a registry back-up link check.

missed_items.topic: AI 8006 exclusions and AI 8013 check characters
missed_items.fact: In the GS1 syntax dictionary AI 8006 excludes AIs 01, 03 and 37, and AI 8013 uses alphanumeric check characters (csumalpha), so a numeric mod-10 routine cannot validate it. AI 01 allows the qualifiers 22, 10, 21 or the alternative 235 path.

LEIs issued before 30 November 2012 do not follow the 4-character LOU prefix rule, and maintenance can move to another LOU without changing the code. An LEI syntax check must not rely on the prefix to identify the current LOU.

python-stdnum latest release is 2.2 (2026-01-04). eclipse-tractusx/digital-product-pass is archived; its latest release is digital-product-pass-4.0.2 (2024-09-13), the last push 2025-09-18. aas-specs-api was pushed 2026-10-16 (after the file's 2026-07-20 file commit) and has release v3.2.0 (2026-07-21).

missed_items.topic: IANA dpp reference points at UNTP page
missed_items.fact: The IANA row for 'dpp' states the description 'a link from a context URI that identifies a product to its digital product passport' and references the UNTP identity resolver anchor. A linkset check can use the registry as an open oracle.

overall: The file is highly reliable on the points checked. All version numbers, statuses and dates of GS1, IDTA, W3C, IANA, NXP, RFC and Catena-X sources match the primary pages, and every repository field (licence, archived flag, push date, release) matches the GitHub API. EU legal citations match the Cellar texts, with two caveats: Implementing Regulation 2026/1778 Art. 10(3) was not seen (only recital 18), and the battery QR code scope should be qualified. Engine mappings (existing_check statements) match the code and capability manifest. Defects found are small: one literature record with year 0 (true year 2024), one missing venue, an overstated 'shared secret' wording for UNTP UUIDs, and the AASd-131 and AASd-133 constraint wording that was not read. No rule 5 problem found. Limits of this check: EUR-Lex HTML was unavailable, so legal texts were read from Cellar windows; PDF page counts rest on PDF metadata.
